facts.quote: Date of service: 03/11/2025
Patient states he was lifting a tote he estimated at 60 pounds when he felt a sharp pain in his low back.
facts.note: This is the patient history; compare the employer weight without treating the report as proof.

facts.quote: Pain 7/10 in the low back, no radiation.
Patient denies any prior back injury or back pain.
facts.note: The denial conflicts with the later history of a prior strain.

facts.quote: Straight leg raise negative bilaterally.
facts.note: The negative emergency examination can be contrasted with the later positive finding.

facts.quote: Lumbar spine x-ray, three views, ordered; report to follow.
Diagnosis: acute lumbar strain.
Off work for 3 days, then return as tolerated.
Patient reports a lumbar strain in 2019 after moving furniture, resolved with rest.
facts.note: Prior symptoms may support a different explanation.

facts.quote: Restrictions: no lifting over 10 pounds and no repetitive bending through 04/11/2025.
Referred to physical therapy, two visits per week for six weeks.
Lumbar flexion 40 degrees, extension 10 degrees.
Patient reports new numbness into the left calf since approximately 04/10/2025.
Recommend MRI of the lumbar spine before further progression.
Discharge summary to follow at visit 12.
L4-L5: 4 mm posterior central disc protrusion contacting the thecal sac.
Positive straight leg raise on the left at 45 degrees.
Impression: L4-L5 disc protrusion with left L5 radiculopathy.
Plan: left L4-L5 transforaminal epidural steroid injection.
In my opinion the L4-L5 disc protrusion is causally related to the lifting injury of 03/11/2025 described by the patient, within a reasonable degree of medical probability.
The patient has not reached maximum medical improvement.
Employee reported lifting a tote weighing approximately 40 pounds from a floor pallet.
facts.note: The employer and emergency histories differ on the tote weight.

facts.quote: Average weekly wage: $912.40
The L4-L5 findings are degenerative and pre-existing, not causally related to the work incident of 03/11/2025.
The examinee is at maximum medical improvement as of today's examination.
No work restrictions are indicated.
Restrictions: sedentary duty, no lifting over 15 pounds, until re-evaluation on 06/20/2025.
No further treatment is medically necessary.
Lumbar strain, likely work related.
Date of hire: 08/02/2021
Lift up to 50 pounds repeatedly during the shift.
There is mild degenerative change noted at the lower vertebral levels.
facts.note: Degeneration offers a possible defense explanation; reserve medicine for our expert.

facts.quote: Range of motion (ROM) in the lumbar spine is limited in flexion.
Strength testing of lower extremities is 5/5 bilaterally.
Reflexes are 2+ and symmetric in all tested segments.
Sensation is intact to light touch throughout the dermatomes.
Straight leg raise negative bilaterally.
No objective findings of radiculopathy on today's examination.
